sources.source: Stripe — "Receive Stripe events in your webhook endpoint"

items.item: Stripe doesn't guarantee the delivery of events in the order that they're generated.

at.step: Reveal: an event id beats a timestamp for dedup

items.item: Webhook endpoints might occasionally receive the same event more than once; guard against this by logging processed event IDs, not timestamps.

items.item: Stripe attempts to deliver events for up to three days with exponential backoff in live mode.

items.item: This topic leaves out the design method's own answers to these questions (topics 1-9), destination-side questions (topic 11), and the ingestion, CDC, contract, and classification mechanics themselves.
A source interview and measurement-over-adjective are established design practice, not an emerging technique.
This topic gives the shop what goes into the pipeline; the next topic (destination-side interrogation) gives what has to come out, which most changes the design.
The maintenance cost of connectors grows with source count: each new source is a connector to build, monitor, and upgrade, which is the real cost of "just one more source".
